records.lesson_subject: IPv6 PIM-SM Bootstrap Router (BSR) and dynamic Rendezvous Point discovery
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: PIM6 BSR candidate election and BSR advertisement carry candidate-RP set; routers learn RP-to-group mappings dynamically; optional static RP and per-VRF global settings remain distinct.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Receiver joins IPv6 group; PIM-SM routers use BSR-distributed RP mapping for shared-tree registration and later source-tree transition; candidate priority/hash and group ACL constrain mapping.
records.failure_class: No RP mapping, wrong RP/group scope, BSR not elected/reachable, or VRF-scoped control-plane mismatch.
records.evidence_pattern: PIM6 BSR router, RP mapping, RP hash, multicast route and MLD group outputs; verify control-plane mapping separately from receiver membership and data-plane forwarding.
records.remediation_path: Enable multicast routing and PIM6 on participating interfaces; configure BSR interface/candidate and candidate-RP group/priority; verify BSR and RP mappings per VRF; use static RP only as an intentional fallback.
records.question_fingerprint: Distinguish receiver MLD membership from BSR election and RP mapping; infer which control-plane object is missing.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three-router IPv6 multicast topology: two BSR/RP candidates, one receiver edge; BSR advertisements, RP-set mapping, shared tree and receiver branch.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Earlier multicast TTL and IPv4/IPv6 group forwarding lessons do not cover PIM6 BSR election or dynamic RP discovery.

records.lesson_subject: Local certificate template validity, managed-device renewal and expiry notifications
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Per-ADOM FortiManager local CA signs device-generated CSRs; Local certificate templates define validity; Certificate Operations renews selected device certificates; expiry notification identifies managed-device certificates within 30 days.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create Local template -> device generates CSR during VPN topology install -> FortiManager CA signs -> certificate and CA public certificate installed -> later renew selected device certificates from Certificate Operations.
records.failure_class: Expired/near-expiry device certificate, wrong template type, missing Feature Visibility, or mismatch between device certificate and CA trust.
records.evidence_pattern: Template Type/Validity, certificate operations device list/expiry dates, notification count and per-device certificate details; these prove inventory/renewal state but not successful peer trust until the installed chain is verified.
records.remediation_path: Enable Certificate feature visibility; use Local template when FortiManager-managed validity/renewal is required; confirm correct ADOM and device selection; renew, then verify the installed certificate chain and VPN authentication.
records.question_fingerprint: Identify Local versus External template capability, 30-day notification boundary, and CSR signing sequence.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager per-ADOM CA, certificate template, FortiGate CSR, signed leaf/CA certificate install, expiry alert and renewal loop.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiManager lessons cover ADOM/workspace and install workflows; certificate lifecycle automation is not in the 216 lesson inventory.

records.lesson_subject: Machine-learning anomaly detection: historical training, artifact validation and live inference
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: mlflow builds model artifacts from historical logs for login-anomaly, traffic-download-anomaly and traffic-upload-anomaly; model training/testing and artifact deployment are separate from scheduled inference.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable global mlflow -> enable a model -> train on configured historical days -> test on held-out days/sensitivity -> deploy artifact -> inference evaluates tracked assets at model-specific interval -> predefined alert handler surfaces deviations.
records.failure_class: No artifacts, insufficient or unrepresentative history, model never deployed, asset cap/exclusion, training/test failure, or inference cadence too slow.
records.evidence_pattern: diagnose mlflow config/training-status/list-artifacts/show-assets/test-result/infer-result; alert handler details; distinguish trained artifact from deployed artifact and generated alert.
records.remediation_path: Confirm model status and data history; train/test with adequate assets; inspect excluded assets and sensitivity; deploy validated artifact; choose model-specific inference interval; verify alerts in All Alerts.
records.question_fingerprint: Distinguish model, asset and artifact; identify whether training, validation, deployment or inference is the failed stage.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Historical logs -> model/asset selection -> training artifact -> held-out test -> deployment -> periodic inference -> anomaly alert.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiAnalyzer lessons cover event handlers, FortiAI alert triage, log ingestion and archive; none covers mlflow behavioral baselines/artifact lifecycle.

records.lesson_subject: Per-application OpenSSL security levels and compatibility override from tunnel mode
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 defaults OpenSSL security level to 2 (previously 0); CLI can set 0-5 globally via default or per application daemon; tunnel-mode compatible overrides level to 0 on the switch where applied, strict uses configured per-app level.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: A FortiSwitch application daemon initiates/accepts TLS or SSH using OpenSSL policy; negotiated protocol/cipher/certificate strength is constrained by effective security level; tunnel-mode compatibility may override that policy.
records.failure_class: After upgrade, legacy peer certificate/cipher/protocol rejected; one daemon fails while other switch services work; apparent per-app setting overridden by tunnel-mode.
records.evidence_pattern: get configuration under config system security app-security; inspect switch-controller tunnel-mode; correlate daemon-specific TLS handshake/logs; successful SSH/HTTPS from one service does not prove every daemon uses same policy.
records.remediation_path: Identify failing application and peer requirements; use strict mode for configured per-app levels; set a narrow per-app exception only when justified; avoid lowering default globally; retest handshake and revert temporary exception.
records.question_fingerprint: Determine effective OpenSSL level when tunnel-mode=compatible and identify why per-application TLS behavior differs.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin CLI -> global/per-daemon OpenSSL security-level policy -> application TLS/SSH client/server -> remote peer; separate tunnel-mode override branch.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Signed firmware-image verification is an artifact-integrity feature, not runtime OpenSSL protocol/cipher policy. The recent Community backup-transfer article is only an operational scenario companion, not the primary lesson.

records.lesson_subject: IPsec offload for encrypted CAPWAP data channels
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: CAPWAP control channel is always DTLS-encrypted; client-data channel can be clear-text, DTLS, IPsec or IPsec with serial-number binding; ipsec-offload controls FortiAP-side IPsec traffic offload and defaults enabled for IPsec policies.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiAP joins FortiGate -> CAPWAP control channel established -> WTP profile selects data-channel security -> IPsec data tunnel carries client packets -> FortiAP performs offload when enabled.
records.failure_class: CAPWAP control is up but data channel fails/underperforms; wrong DTLS policy; IPsec negotiation/serial-number binding issue; AP CPU bottleneck.
records.evidence_pattern: WTP profile dtls-policy and ipsec-offload, CAPWAP control state, IPsec SA/packet counters and throughput/CPU; control-channel health alone does not prove data-channel encryption or offload.
records.remediation_path: Verify supported AP/FortiOS model and profile; select ipsec-vpn or ipsec-vpn-sn; verify tunnel and traffic counters; confirm AP-side offload; compare AP CPU and throughput; do not weaken control-channel DTLS.
records.question_fingerprint: Distinguish control-channel DTLS from data-channel IPsec and identify the device doing the offload.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wireless clients -> FortiAP -> CAPWAP control DTLS plus separate IPsec data channel -> FortiGate; AP-side offload callout.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior wireless lessons cover MLO, roaming, RadSec, packet capture and VAP/VLAN behaviors; none covers CAPWAP data-channel IPsec offload.

records.lesson_subject: Windows AV compliance through the Windows Security-Center provider
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 adds a Windows AV category choice named Security-Center alongside the prior Defender-specific check; endpoint AV status/signature freshness becomes a compliance input.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Windows endpoint agent/host data reports AV state -> FortiNAC evaluates Windows AV category against host profile/compliance policy -> host state and access action follow configured policy.
records.failure_class: Defender-specific check gives false noncompliance for endpoints protected by another Windows Security Center-registered AV provider, or endpoint AV definitions are stale.
records.evidence_pattern: Host/agent-reported Windows AV category and definition freshness compared with host-profile requirement; the release note does not document the Windows API or exact agent polling interval, so do not infer those from the setting name.
records.remediation_path: Use Security-Center for endpoints whose active AV provider is registered with Windows Security Center; validate agent reporting and host profile; compare endpoint provider state and FortiNAC host compliance before changing enforcement.
records.question_fingerprint: Choose Defender-specific versus Security-Center compliance source and identify what evidence is documented versus unspecified.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Windows endpoint AV provider -> Windows Security Center -> FortiNAC endpoint/agent observation -> host profile compliance decision -> access state.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiNAC lessons cover MDM, patch-management and RADIUS identity; AV-provider compliance source is a distinct endpoint posture input.

records.lesson_subject: KEA DHCP for isolated hosts and PXE boot option delivery
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6 replaces legacy ISC DHCP with KEA DHCP for internal isolated-host address assignment; custom DHCP options are configured through supported GUI attributes rather than direct root edits to dhcp.conf.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Isolated host broadcasts DHCP Discover -> KEA scope on isolation interface offers address and options -> client receives next-server/boot-file-name/TFTP details -> client fetches network boot program from TFTP server.
records.failure_class: Lease succeeds but PXE boot fails because boot server/filename options are missing, inconsistent, or file/TFTP/firewall reachability is wrong.
records.evidence_pattern: DHCP lease/address and scope; configured Next Server, Boot File Name, tftp-server-name and boot-file-name; KEA config and lease file; successful DHCP ACK does not prove TFTP reachability or NBP execution.
records.remediation_path: Use GUI DHCP attributes; configure both Advanced Next Server/Boot File Name and standard options when clients require both; verify BIOS PXE, TFTP file permissions, isolation-to-TFTP firewall policy and actual transfer.
records.question_fingerprint: Distinguish DHCP address assignment from PXE option delivery and TFTP retrieval; identify why a host has an address but cannot boot.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Isolated endpoint -> KEA DHCP on FortiNAC-F -> lease plus PXE options -> TFTP file server -> boot program execution; firewall path annotated.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiNAC-F topics cover NetFlow, HA, host learning and vulnerability scanners; no KEA internal DHCP/PXE workflow in published lessons.

records.lesson_subject: OTP-only push notification mode and FortiClient-compatible fallback
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: User Account Policies define OTP-Only Push mode: None, Normal or FortiClient-compatible; when an OTP-only account lacks push capability, Normal rejects while FortiClient-compatible ignores that push trigger to allow manual username+OTP retry.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: RADIUS/remote auth request identifies OTP-only user -> push trigger is processed per account policy and account push capability -> push accepted or rejected/ignored -> FortiClient manual OTP retry path only in compatible mode.
records.failure_class: OTP-only login fails for users without push support; push delivery outage; client expects manual OTP fallback but policy mode rejects instead.
records.evidence_pattern: User Account Policies > General selected mode, account push capability, RADIUS challenge/reject/timeout behavior and subsequent manual OTP request; no push notification is not itself proof of invalid OTP.
records.remediation_path: Select Normal when unsupported push should fail closed; choose FortiClient-compatible only for supported clients requiring manual OTP fallback; verify account token/push registration and capture the complete challenge sequence.
records.question_fingerprint: Predict whether an OTP-only user without push capability is rejected or allowed to retry manually under each mode.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Authentication request -> OTP-only policy mode -> push-capable branch; unsupported-push branch -> reject or ignore -> manual OTP retry.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiAuthenticator lessons cover SAML, RADIUS attributes, FSSO, OAuth and certificate authorities; OTP-only push fallback is not present.

records.lesson_subject: Per-interface TCP Segmentation Offload (TSO) and Generic Segmentation Offload (GSO)
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 enables TSO and GSO by default on system interfaces; kernel/NIC defers segmentation of large transmit buffers into wire-sized TCP segments; CLI controls each interface independently.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Application creates large TCP payload -> stack queues GSO/TSO buffer -> NIC/kernel segments for wire MTU -> peer receives ordinary TCP segments; capture point may see pre-segmentation super-packets.
records.failure_class: CPU overhead or throughput regression when offload disabled; packet capture appears to show oversized packets; per-interface asymmetry causes different results on separate paths.
records.evidence_pattern: Per-interface `get`/configuration for tso/gso, CPU/throughput counters, capture location and on-wire packet sizes; host-side capture may show offload artifacts that are not present on the wire.
records.remediation_path: Check interface-specific TSO/GSO settings; compare a capture at the sender and an external tap; temporarily disable one feature on a test interface only if diagnosing a suspected offload issue; restore defaults after test.
records.question_fingerprint: Distinguish host-stack super-packet capture from on-wire segmentation and identify the correct per-interface control.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM application/TCP stack -> GSO/TSO large buffer -> NIC/kernel segmentation -> physical link -> peer; capture before and after segmentation.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: No prior FortiPAM lesson covers packet segmentation/offload or packet-capture interpretation.

records.lesson_subject: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials grant for public REST API tokens
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM 7.5.1 API tokens support OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials grant; Client ID and Client Secret obtain a short-lived Bearer access token; token privileges inherit the creating user's role and organization scope; revoke invalidates in-use access token immediately.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Authorized org user creates API token -> client posts grant_type=client_credentials, client_id and client_secret to token endpoint -> access_token/expires_in returned -> REST calls use Bearer token -> reissue on expiry while secret valid or reset secret/revoke token.
records.failure_class: Token creation permission missing, wrong organization context, insufficient inherited role privileges, expired secret/access token or revoked token.
records.evidence_pattern: API token table (owner/org/client ID/secret expiry/status), OAuth token response, HTTP authorization result and target API authorization; successful token issuance does not prove requested endpoint privilege.
records.remediation_path: Grant OAuth Tokens permission to intended role; create token while logged in to target organization; protect client secret; request new access token on expiry; reset secret or revoke compromised token; verify role and org scope.
records.question_fingerprint: Differentiate access-token expiry, client-secret expiry, organization scope and inherited role privilege.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSIEM org-scoped user/role -> API token client credentials -> OAuth token endpoint -> Bearer token -> REST API authorization -> resource.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiSIEM lessons cover collectors, parsers, event correlation, CMDB and AWS ingestion; OAuth client-credentials API token lifecycle is distinct.

records.lesson_subject: Secure Browser extension profiles, user assignment and browser-side data controls
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Managed Chrome/Edge Secure Browser extension enforces client-side dynamic page inspection and FortiGuard category/domain rules without relying solely on network DPI; profiles map users/groups using IdP attributes (email required) and define sensitive-input, download and site-specific overrides.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User signs in to browser extension -> IdP attributes matched to Secure Browser assignment rule -> profile applies dynamic inspection/category/domain overrides -> browser action (sensitive input/download) is allowed, warned or blocked.
records.failure_class: Extension unavailable/disabled in private browsing, user not assigned due to missing email claim, feature not enabled on tenant, or URL override precedence produces unexpected action.
records.evidence_pattern: Tenant feature availability, extension installation/state, IdP email/group attributes, assigned profile, category rule and URL domain group override; network DPI logs alone do not prove browser-side control.
records.remediation_path: Confirm select-availability enablement; install supported Chrome/Edge extension; ensure email claim and group mapping; validate profile assignment and rule precedence; enable extension in private mode only if that mode is allowed.
records.question_fingerprint: Trace profile assignment and distinguish dynamic page inspection from category lookups and URL domain overrides.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IdP attributes -> user assignment rule -> Secure Browser profile -> dynamic page inspection/category rule -> URL override -> browser action.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior FortiSASE lessons cover CASB, DEM, PoP selection, posture tags and tunnel steering; browser-extension enforcement is a distinct endpoint control plane.

records.lesson_subject: Graceful BGP shutdown for planned SD-WAN edge maintenance
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 implements RFC 8326 graceful BGP shutdown: initiator marks routes with GSHUT community and signals shutdown; receiver lowers local preference for affected routes; persistent shutdown/graceful-soft controls and delay support orderly drain.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Maintenance operator initiates graceful shutdown on edge neighbor -> route advertisements carry GSHUT community -> peer applies lower local preference and selects alternate path -> delay allows traffic drain before session closure.
records.failure_class: Peer does not recognize/propagate GSHUT community, local-preference policy does not match, alternate path absent, or shutdown delay expires before traffic drains.
records.evidence_pattern: Neighbor state, advertised/received communities, route-map/policy local preference, best-path change and traffic counters; BGP session down alone does not prove traffic drained.
records.remediation_path: Configure matching initiator and receiver behavior; preserve community through route policy; verify alternate route and SD-WAN member/overlay health; observe traffic shift before completing shutdown.
records.question_fingerprint: Distinguish graceful shutdown from graceful restart and determine why the peer did not de-prefer the maintenance path.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: SD-WAN edge A (initiator) -> BGP GSHUT community -> edge B (receiver) lowers local preference -> alternate overlay/underlay path takes traffic -> maintenance shutdown.
records.nearest_inventory_comparison: Prior BGP lessons cover neighbor transport, community-to-route-tag translation and route selection; none covers RFC 8326 GSHUT drain behavior.
